prompt:
ATTACHED IMAGES
2 images are attached to this request, in this order. They are referred to below by number.
Image 1 (Subject image) is the main subject. Treat it as the exact source, not as inspiration. Use the real person or object from this photograph exactly as it appears. Keep the identity, face and facial structure, expression, hairstyle, body shape and proportions, pose, clothing, accessories and every distinguishing detail unchanged. You may cut it out from its original background, scale it evenly, and crop or position it as the layout requires. Do not distort, stretch, squash, warp, reshape, redraw, retouch, beautify, age or de-age it. Do not replace it with a similar-looking person or object, and do not add or remove details. Keep its original, natural colours, skin tones and lighting.

Image 2 (Background image) is the main subject. Treat it as the exact source, not as inspiration. Use the real person or object from this photograph exactly as it appears. Keep the identity, face and facial structure, expression, hairstyle, body shape and proportions, pose, clothing, accessories and every distinguishing detail unchanged. You may cut it out from its original background, scale it evenly, and crop or position it as the layout requires. Do not distort, stretch, squash, warp, reshape, redraw, retouch, beautify, age or de-age it. Do not replace it with a similar-looking person or object, and do not add or remove details. Keep its original, natural colours, skin tones and lighting.

Use the attached subject image (image 1) as the primary visual source and the attached background image (image 2) as the secondary visual source.

Create a fixed square 1:1 retro editorial collage that closely follows the supplied reference structure: a large isolated photographic subject layered over a rigid field of evenly spaced circular graphic modules on a warm off-white paper background. The result should feel like a mid-century modernist editorial poster reconstructed through cut-paper photomontage, halftone printing, photocopy texture, and restrained geometric design.

INPUT REFERENCES

PRIMARY CONTENT:
the attached subject image (image 1)

SECONDARY CONTENT:
the attached background image (image 2)

HIGHLIGHT CIRCLE COLOUR:
#E03013

The subject image controls the identity and form of the main foreground element.

The background image provides visual fragments used selectively inside the non-highlight circular modules.

Do not borrow people, objects, identities, clothing, architecture, or literal content from the style reference. The reference controls only the composition, graphic system, print treatment, layering, scale relationships, and overall aesthetic.

SUBJECT / PRIMARY-CONTENT PRESERVATION

Use the attached subject image (image 1) as the dominant foreground element. The subject may be a person, animal, vehicle, product, sculpture, object, building, or other recognizable form.

Preserve its important identifying characteristics, including recognizable identity, facial structure when applicable, expression when applicable, hairstyle when applicable, clothing and accessories when applicable, silhouette, body or object proportions, pose or orientation, structural details, materials and surface characteristics, and distinguishing visual features.

Do not redesign, replace, or reinterpret the subject into a different object or person.

Remove the original background surrounding the subject and treat it as an isolated photographic cutout.

Convert the subject predominantly into black, charcoal, grey, and faded off-white photographic tones while retaining enough internal detail for immediate recognition.

The subject treatment should resemble a photograph reproduced through an old editorial printing process rather than a clean modern grayscale conversion.

Apply moderately strong black-and-white contrast, slightly crushed dark tones, restrained grey midtones, softly compressed highlights, subtle halftone dots, photocopy grain, faint ink breakup, lightly distressed cutout edges, and slight newsprint softness.

Keep important facial features, textures, contours, and structural details readable.

COMPOSITION

The output must ALWAYS be square 1:1.

Build the composition around a regular geometric matrix of evenly sized circular modules.

Use approximately 5 circles across each row and approximately 4–5 rows vertically, creating the impression of a disciplined modernist dot grid.

The circles should be approximately equal in diameter, use consistent horizontal and vertical spacing, remain visually aligned to an invisible grid, extend across most of the square canvas, leave comfortable off-white negative space around the outer edges, and remain clearly visible around the foreground subject.

Do not make the circle arrangement random, chaotic, or decorative. It should feel systematic and editorial.

Place the subject large near the center, generally occupying roughly 45–65% of the image height depending on its natural proportions.

Allow the subject to overlap several circles. The subject should sit visually in front of the circle grid, clearly establishing foreground-background hierarchy.

The subject does not need to be perfectly centered. A subtle offset is encouraged when it improves balance, similar to an editorial cutout manually placed over a printed grid.

Do not crop important parts of the subject unnecessarily. When the source contains a complete object or full figure, preserve as much of the complete silhouette as reasonably possible.

Maintain generous negative space. Avoid filling every gap with additional decoration.

BACKGROUND / SECONDARY-CONTENT TREATMENT

Use the attached background image (image 2) only inside selected non-highlight circles.

Never display the attached background image (image 2) as a complete rectangular background scene.

Instead, break the background image into individual circular crops distributed across the grid.

Each image-containing circle should function like a small circular window showing a different crop or fragment from the attached background image (image 2).

Vary the crop naturally across circles so the same background image appears fragmented across the composition.

The fragments may include architectural details, landscape fragments, objects, textures, environmental details, structural shapes, and recognizable portions of the supplied background image.

Do not reconstruct the complete background scene across the circles like a puzzle. The fragments should feel independently cropped and editorially sampled.

Process the background-image fragments heavily so they remain secondary to the subject.

Apply muted contrast, reduced saturation, warm cream-biased printing, halftone dot texture, faded ink, slight image degradation, coarse printed character, subtle photocopy wear, and gentle tonal flattening.

Some circles may become extremely faded or nearly monochromatic so that the grid contains a mixture of visible image fragments and quiet pale printed modules.

HIGHLIGHT CIRCLE SYSTEM

Distribute a smaller number of solid highlight circles throughout the grid using #E03013.

These circles are mandatory visual anchors.

Apply #E03013 as a fully opaque, visually obvious flat printed colour.

The highlight circles must remain completely solid, contain no photographic imagery, contain no background-image fragments, contain no gradients, contain no internal illustrations, use the same diameter as the other grid circles, appear scattered rhythmically throughout the grid, and remain visually distinct from the muted image-filled circles.

Use approximately one highlight circle for every two to four secondary circles.

Avoid obvious checkerboards, stripes, perfect symmetry, or repetitive alternating patterns. The distribution should feel deliberately irregular while still respecting the underlying grid.

Several highlight circles may be partially obscured by the foreground subject.

The difference between the solid highlight circles, muted background-image circles, and grayscale foreground subject is fundamental to the design and must be visually obvious at a glance.

STYLE MATCHING

Match the supplied reference through the following visual characteristics: retro modernist editorial layout, late-mid-century print-design influence, geometric circle-grid composition, photographic cut-paper foreground subject, minimal photomontage, screen-printed or offset-printed appearance, halftone reproduction, photocopy degradation, imperfect analog ink, matte paper surface, restrained use of colour, high use of negative space, and slightly handmade physical collage quality.

Avoid a polished digital advertising aesthetic. Avoid hyper-clean vector perfection. The result should feel tactile, printed, slightly aged, and editorial.

COLOUR TREATMENT

Use a warm ivory, antique white, or pale cream paper tone for the full canvas.

The foreground subject remains predominantly grayscale.

The secondary circular fragments derived from the attached background image (image 2) should be significantly muted, faded, and warmed so they integrate with the cream paper.

Use #E03013 only for the bold solid accent circles.

The colour separation is mandatory and must be visually obvious at a glance:
1. grayscale photographic foreground subject
2. vivid solid #E03013 circles
3. pale, muted, halftone background-image circles
4. warm off-white paper base

Do not recolour the entire composition with the highlight colour. Do not tint the main subject with the highlight colour.

LIGHTING AND TONAL TREATMENT

Preserve the underlying lighting information of the attached subject image (image 1) sufficiently to maintain form and dimensionality.

Do not introduce dramatic cinematic relighting.

Flatten the subject slightly through the printing treatment while keeping readable shadow and highlight structure.

Use matte blacks rather than glossy blacks, dark charcoal shadows, compressed midtones, subdued highlights, minimal specular shine, and restrained dynamic range.

The background circle fragments should have even lower contrast than the subject.

The subject must remain the sharpest and most visually dominant component.

TEXTURE AND FINISHING

Apply a unified analog print finish across the composition.

Include subtle warm paper grain, fine paper fibers, halftone dots, photocopy speckling, imperfect ink density, slight ink bleeding, faint registration irregularity, distressed photographic edges, tiny tonal inconsistencies, and soft archival wear.

Keep these effects refined enough that the image remains clean and intentional.

Do not cover the artwork with heavy scratches, grunge, stains, folds, or extreme damage.

The paper should remain relatively clean with understated age and print imperfections.

STRICT REQUIREMENTS

Output is ALWAYS square 1:1. Use the attached subject image (image 1) as the only source for the foreground subject. Preserve the recognizable identity and structure of the subject. Isolate the subject from its original background. Render the subject primarily as a black-and-white photographic cutout. Keep the subject large and dominant near the center. Build the background from a structured grid of equal-sized circles. Keep circle diameter and spacing consistent. Use the attached background image (image 2) only as fragmented content inside non-highlight circles. Never show the attached background image (image 2) as one complete rectangular scene. Apply halftone and faded-print treatment to the background-image circles. Use #E03013 for selected solid circles. Highlight circles must remain completely solid and opaque. Never place background imagery inside the highlight circles. Allow the foreground subject to overlap the circle grid. Maintain clear depth: subject in front, circles behind. Use a warm cream/off-white paper background. Preserve generous negative space. Maintain visible analog print texture. Keep the design minimal, graphic, balanced, and poster-like. No typography is permitted.

AVOID / NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS

Do not include text, typography, letters, numbers, captions, labels, logos, watermarks, UI elements, borders, decorative frames, arrows, icons, infographics, charts, diagrams, excessive geometric shapes other than the circle system, squares or rectangles competing with the circle grid, photographic rectangular background panels, full-scene display of the attached background image (image 2), image content inside solid highlight circles, gradients inside highlight circles, glossy 3D circles, shadows behind individual circles, bevels, metallic effects, neon effects, excessive saturation, excessive grunge, heavy paper damage, overly dramatic lighting, cinematic lens effects, fake depth-of-field blur, modern glossy advertising treatment, complex decorative backgrounds, duplicated subjects, distorted anatomy, altered identity, or unnecessary cropping of the main subject.

The final result should read immediately as a restrained retro editorial photomontage: one dominant grayscale photographic cutout floating over a disciplined matrix of pale halftone image circles and vivid solid highlight circles on warm archival paper.

ADDITIONAL RULES
- Use the subject from the attached image exactly as photographed. Do not distort, stretch, warp, redraw, retouch or replace it, and do not change its identity, features or proportions.
